aliases: His Majesty's Royal Palace and Fortress of the Tower of London

claims.text: The Tower of London is a historic castle and fortress founded in 1066 by William the Conqueror during the Norman Conquest.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The massive White Tower at its centre was built in 1078 and originally served as a deeply resented symbol of Norman oppression.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Over its incredible history, the complex has served as an armoury, a menagerie for exotic animals, and the heavily guarded home of the Crown Jewels of England.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It became infamous as a prison in the 16th and 17th centuries, holding disgraced figures and even Elizabeth I before she became queen.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Despite its terrifying reputation as a place of death, only seven people were actually executed inside the Tower before the 20th century.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The very first prisoner held here in 1100 was also the first to escape, managing to climb down using a rope smuggled inside a butt of wine.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, during the winter months, visitors can actually go ice skating on the bottom of the castle's old dry moat.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: While you can take pictures almost everywhere, photography is strictly forbidden inside St John's Chapel in the White Tower.
claims.subject: self
